ai.description: *Cyrtodactylus chamba* reaches 78 mm SVL. It is brownish with five dark dorsal bands and a yellow-spotted head. Distinguishing features include a series of enlarged femoral scales and 18–20 subdigital lamellae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus chamba* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous dark nuchal loop that connects the posterior corners of the eyes.
ai.habitat: *Cyrtodactylus chamba* inhabits rocky crevices and stone walls within subtropical broadleaf forests at elevations ranging from approximately 800 to 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Chamba bent-toed gecko is strictly nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates on rock surfaces and vertical structures within its habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cyrtodactylus chamba* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two eggs. Its breeding season occurs during the monsoon months, typically from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Chamba Bent-toed Gecko is endemic to the Chamba district of Himachal Pradesh in the western Himalayas, occurring at elevations between 800 and 1,200 meters.
